entry_state: Receiving all hedged inventory transfers its attached reserve directly into cost, without new cash or income. Subsequent sales and write-downs track a homogeneous batch's gross cost and allowance, not another hedge-reserve release. The partial-sale example now derives proportional allowance removal before the next valuation.
exit_state: Inventory sales remove only the sold goods' allowance; recovery concerns goods still held. Net currency hedges retain gross sales, expenses and their recognition periods, with separate hedge presentation and reserve timing. The next section turns from hedging to employee award conditions, settlement rights and earnings participation.
findings: After selling 26 impaired units, only allowance 680 remains available for reversal; the full expense history still totals the original adjusted cost 10800.
The two-period net hedge has first-period profit 100 and OCI 8, then profit −80 and OCI −8. Lifetime profit 20 alone would not validate those periods.
The nil-position example requires four eligibility conditions; equal gross totals alone do not establish qualification.
